title: Codebusters B 2027
summary: Fifty minutes, three team members, and a packet of ciphertext to break. The rules name every cipher type that can appear at Division B, and the first question is timed. This course takes them one at a time, with the cryptanalysis that opens each.
objectives: Open a monoalphabetic substitution with frequency, pattern and contact analysis in English and in Spanish
Decrypt with a given key for Caesar, Atbash, Porta, Baconian, Nihilist and the checkerboard without slips
Cryptanalyse Porta, Nihilist, checkerboard, homophonic, Fractionated Morse and complete columnar transposition from a crib
Solve a base-10 cryptarithm and read the message off its mapping
Split a packet across three people and decide when a question is not worth the time

units.title: What Cryptanalysis Actually Is
units.summary: Every question on this exam is a decryption, and most give you less than a key. The tools are frequency, pattern and the crib.
objectives: Use English and Spanish letter frequencies to open a substitution
Use a crib to anchor a cipher you cannot brute force

lessons.title: Plaintext, Ciphertext, Key
lessons.objective: Define plaintext, ciphertext and key, and state what an attacker knows under Kerckhoffs's principle.

lessons.title: Substitution Changes Letters, Transposition Moves Them
lessons.objective: Decide from a ciphertext's letter frequencies alone whether it is a substitution or a transposition, and explain why the test works.

lessons.title: Frequency Analysis in English
lessons.objective: Use single letter, bigram and trigram frequencies to make first guesses at a monoalphabetic substitution.

lessons.title: Patterns, Short Words and the Crib
lessons.objective: Use word length, repeated letter patterns and a supplied crib to place letters in a partly solved cryptogram.

lessons.title: K1 Alphabets and Random Alphabets
lessons.objective: Explain what an ACA K1 alphabet is, how a keyword builds it, and how that constrains the solution compared with a random alphabet.

units.title: Aristocrats, Patristocrats and Xenocrypts
units.summary: The timed question is an Aristocrat. No letter ever decrypts to itself in any of these three.
objectives: Work a Patristocrat without word boundaries

lessons.title: Aristocrats: Spaces Included
lessons.objective: Solve an Aristocrat by combining frequency, short words and pattern words, and use the no-letter-maps-to-itself rule to eliminate candidates.

lessons.title: Solving the Timed Aristocrat Fast
lessons.objective: Work an Aristocrat in a fixed order that gets to a readable fragment quickly, and know when to signal.

lessons.title: Patristocrats: Spaces Removed, Grouped in Fives
lessons.objective: Solve a Patristocrat encoded on a K1 alphabet without word boundaries, relying on frequency and contact rather than word shape.

lessons.title: Xenocrypts: Spanish on an English Keyword Alphabet
lessons.objective: Solve a Spanish cryptogram using Spanish letter frequencies, common Spanish short words, and the accented and ñ conventions.

lessons.title: Homophonic Substitution
lessons.objective: Decrypt a homophonic cipher given a crib naming at least three letters of a four-unique-letter keyword, and explain why homophones flatten frequency.

units.title: Caesar, Atbash, Porta and Baconian
units.summary: Four ciphers whose mechanism is a table or a rule you are given, and whose difficulty is entirely in applying it without slipping.
objectives: Decrypt with a given key quickly and without arithmetic slips
Read a Baconian encoding hidden in typography

lessons.title: The Caesar Shift
lessons.objective: Decrypt a Caesar cipher by trying shifts systematically, and express the shift as modular arithmetic on letter positions.

lessons.title: Atbash: the Alphabet Reversed
lessons.objective: Decrypt an Atbash cipher in English and explain why Atbash needs no key and is its own inverse.

lessons.title: The Porta Cipher and the Tabula Recta
lessons.objective: Decrypt a Porta cipher using the Porta table and a given key, and cryptanalyse one from a crib of at least three characters.

lessons.title: Baconian: Two Symbols Hiding in Plain Sight
lessons.objective: Decode a Baconian cipher whose a and b values are carried by letters, glyphs, or bold and italic rendering, using the supplied mapping.

units.title: Polybius, Checkerboard, Nihilist and Fractionated Morse
units.summary: Four ciphers that turn letters into coordinates or symbols before doing anything else.
objectives: Build and read a Polybius square from a keyword

lessons.title: The Polybius Square
lessons.objective: Build a 5x5 Polybius square from a key, encode and decode with it, and state what happens to I and J.

lessons.title: The 5x5 Checkerboard
lessons.objective: Decrypt a checkerboard cipher given the Polybius key, and cryptanalyse one built from two five-letter keywords given a crib.

lessons.title: The Nihilist Cipher
lessons.objective: Decrypt a Nihilist cipher given its keys, by subtracting the repeating key from the additive ciphertext numbers.

lessons.title: Fractionated Morse
lessons.objective: Decrypt a Fractionated Morse ciphertext by expanding to Morse, regrouping in threes and reading against the table, using a crib.

lessons.title: Morse Code Itself
lessons.objective: Read and write Morse for the letters and the separator conventions the resource sheet gives.

units.title: Columnar Transposition and Cryptarithms
units.summary: One cipher that moves letters and one puzzle that is not a cipher at all.
objectives: Break a complete columnar transposition of nine columns or fewer
Solve a base-10 cryptarithm and read the message off the mapping

lessons.title: Complete Columnar Transposition
lessons.objective: Decrypt a complete columnar transposition in nine columns or fewer, using a crib at least one shorter than the column count.

lessons.title: Working Out the Columns and the Order
lessons.objective: Use message length and the crib to determine column count and column order before attempting to read the plaintext.

lessons.title: Cryptarithms: Letters That Are Digits
lessons.objective: Solve a base-10 cryptarithm using carry reasoning and the leading-digit rule, then decode the word from the resulting mapping.

units.title: Working the Exam
units.summary: Fifty minutes, three people, a packet you may split, and bonus questions worth chasing.
objectives: Allocate three people across a splittable packet
Decide when to abandon a question

lessons.title: Three People, One Packet
lessons.objective: Split a Codebusters packet across three team members by cipher type and difficulty, and say who takes the timed question.

lessons.title: The Special Bonus Questions
lessons.objective: Identify which questions are marked as special bonus, and decide whether to attempt one given time remaining.

lessons.title: Two Errors Are Allowed, Three Are Not
lessons.objective: Check a decryption for the errors that cost a question, and know the accuracy threshold the timed bonus requires.
